claim: The stages partition optimizer state, then gradients, then parameters.
conditions: Stage definitions; parameter materialization and residency policies require separate accounting.

claim: The historical experimental implementation includes a subset of the paper’s proposed optimizations.
conditions: Version 3 §10 and Table 3; do not reinterpret as an isolated full-parameter-sharding experiment.

claim: Megatron's estimate 8TP/(nX) gives about 83 days for 450B tokens, 1T parameters, 3,072 GPUs at 163 TFLOP/s, consistent with the reported 84.
conditions: Uses the paper's own measured X; excludes failures, restarts and evaluation unless X covers them.

claim: Transformers 4.51.3 shifts causal-LM labels inside the loss (pad one -100, drop the first label), upcasts logits to FP32 and averages over non-ignored targets unless num_items_in_batch is given.
conditions: Release 4.51.3 source; other releases may differ.

claim: The 4.51.3 Trainer computes num_items_in_batch only when the model accepts loss kwargs (forward has **kwargs or accepts_loss_kwargs) or a compute_loss_func is given; it then counts labels.ne(-100) over all of a step's microbatches on unshifted labels, and with average_tokens_across_devices sums the count over ranks and multiplies the loss by the number of processes.
conditions: Source inspection of trainer.py (get_batch_samples, compute_loss, __init__) plus an executed run of Trainer 4.51.3 / accelerate 1.6.0 on a one-layer LlamaForCausalLM with two 6-token rows and gradient_accumulation_steps=2: num_items_in_batch was 10 against 8 shifted targets. The overcount is one per row whose first label is not -100, so the ratio varies across steps.

claim: PyTorch 2.6 AdamW shrinks parameters by (1 - lr x weight_decay) before the bias-corrected Adam step; clip_grad_norm_ scales all gradients by min(1, max_norm / (total_norm + 1e-6)).
conditions: Release 2.6.0 source, single-tensor path; checked numerically in the lesson script.

claim: Decoupled weight decay as published scales the decay by the schedule multiplier η_t but not by the learning rate α.
conditions: Algorithm 2 of v3 (ICLR 2019).

claim: Llama 3 uses an attention mask preventing attention between documents in the same sequence; it reports limited impact in standard pre-training and importance for continued pre-training on very long sequences.
conditions: v3 §3.2; qualitative statement, no ablation numbers given in the quoted passage.

claim: Normalizing each microbatch's summed loss by the step's total target count, either before backward or by dividing accumulated summed gradients afterwards, reproduces the token-mean gradient; mean-then-divide accumulation optimizes the mean of microbatch means instead (1.5 versus 2 for illustrative losses [1,1,1] and [3]). The equivalence is mathematical, not bitwise.
conditions: Linearity of the gradient; illustrative losses, checked with autograd in scripts/course/p1_update.py. Floating-point summation order and dropout can make results differ numerically.

claim: At AdamW's first step every coordinate with |g| much larger than eps moves by about the learning rate, independent of the gradient's magnitude. Later steps depend on the gradient history: rescaling the whole history by a positive constant leaves the update unchanged (up to eps), rescaling only the current gradient does not (0.1 versus about 0.093 in the scalar example).
conditions: Bias correction with zero-initialized moments; scalar example with lr 0.1, betas (0.9, 0.99) checked against torch.optim.AdamW 2.6.0 in the script.

claim: In PyTorch 2.6, clip_grad_norm_ with a NaN gradient entry returns a NaN norm and turns all gradients into NaN; with an Inf entry it returns Inf, zeroes finite entries and leaves NaN at the Inf entry; it raises only with error_if_nonfinite=True.
conditions: Executed on torch 2.6.0, single parameter, max_norm 1.0.

claim: A -100 label removes only the direct loss term at that output position; the token's embedding and hidden states still receive gradients through later positions that attend to it.
conditions: Chain rule; scalar averaging example checked with autograd in the script.

claim: FineWeb's pipeline: trafilatura on WARC, URL blocklist, fastText English >= 0.65, Gopher quality and repetition filters (~36T tokens), per-snapshot MinHash (20T), C4 filters without terminal punctuation, three custom filters, email and public-IP anonymization (15T).
MinHash with 5-grams and 14 buckets of 8 hashes matches pairs at Jaccard 0.7/0.75/0.8/0.85 with probability 56%/77%/92%/98.8%, from 1-(1-s^8)^14.
conditions: App. E.1 p. 21; reproduced in scripts/course/p2_corpus.py. The post states the 0.75 and 0.85 values operationally; the formula is in the review.

claim: MinHash signatures are built so that the fraction of agreeing positions estimates the Jaccard similarity of two documents' shingle sets.
conditions: Stated operationally in the post (derivation moved to further reading); Broder 1997.

claim: Global MinHash across 96 snapshots removed up to 90% of old snapshots, left 4T tokens and barely improved results; in 2013-48 the kept ~31B tokens trained a worse model than the deduplicated removed data; per-snapshot dedup left 20T and matched RefinedWeb. The cluster-size explanation is the authors' hypothesis.
conditions: Sec 3.4 pp. 5-6, Figs 3-5; 350B-token ablations at 1.71B.

claim: FineWeb's three custom filters (punctuation-line fraction <= 0.12, duplicated-line characters, short-line fraction >= 0.67) removed ~22% of tokens and raised the aggregate ~1%; C4's terminal-punctuation filter removes ~30%.
conditions: Sec 3.5-3.6 pp. 6-7. Text gives the duplicated-line threshold as 0.1; Table 2 and datatrove use 0.01. Table 2 lists 0.69 for the short-line row; text and code use 0.67.

claim: datatrove 0.10.1 FineWebQualityFilter removes the toy flights page with reason short_line_ratio; the current filter also applies a newline-per-word > 0.3 rule not in the paper; examples/fineweb.py applies all filters before MinHash.
conditions: Executed in a scratch virtualenv with datatrove 0.10.1 from PyPI. The post shows only the short_line_ratio result; the discrepancies are in the review.

claim: datatrove's LanguageFilter (ft176, threshold 0.65) keeps the English toy page (en 0.998) and removes a half-Khmer, half-English page (km 0.852) and a Khmer page (km 0.998).
conditions: Executed with fastText lid.176; scores depend on the model file.

claim: FineWeb-Edu: Llama-3-70B-Instruct scored 460k pages 0-5; a linear head on Snowflake-arctic-embed-m trained on 410k; threshold 3, F1 82% against Llama labels; 1.3T tokens; MMLU 33->37%, ARC 46->57% at 350B tokens; topic and Paloma-domain shifts.
DCLM: resiliparse 24.1 and trafilatura 24.5 CORE against 20.7 for WET (1B-1x); resiliparse ~8x faster; DCLM-Baseline keeps the top 10% by a fastText OH-2.5+ELI5 classifier.
conditions: Sec 4.2 Table 3 p. 8; Sec 4.4 Tables 4-5 pp. 8-9.

claim: datatrove's PIIFormatter replaces emails and public IPv4 addresses with fixed placeholders and leaves names untouched; FineWeb's PII handling is limited to emails and public IPs.
conditions: Executed on a toy sentence; FineWeb Sec 3.7 p. 7 and App. A p. 18.

claim: The FineWeb paper does not describe benchmark decontamination of the corpus and intentionally skips decontamination in its Paloma analysis.
conditions: Full-text search of v2 for 'contamin'; Sec 4.2 p. 9.

claim: With constrained data and a fixed compute budget, training with up to 4 epochs of repeated data gives negligible loss changes compared with unique data; with more repetition the value of added compute decays towards zero.
conditions: Abstract and Fig. 1, p. 1, arXiv v4; models up to 9B parameters and 900B tokens. Used in the post's budget activity and the review's budget confound.

claim: CS336 lecture 14 states there is no single optimal filtering threshold (longer training wants more, lower-quality data; shorter training wants less, higher-quality data) and shows a product description repeated 61,036 times in C4.
conditions: lecture_14.py at stanford-cs336/lectures de53a9f, functions filtering() and deduplication(); lecture file read, video not watched.

claim: Contamination is exposure to evaluation items, their answers or solutions, or close derivatives; learning general facts that a benchmark also tests is not contamination. Word-overlap search catches copies but cannot separate general knowledge from reworded items (1/6 shared 3-grams for both in the toy).
conditions: Definition per the series' writing guide; toy overlap counts in scripts/course/p2_corpus.py. FineWeb (Sec 4.2) is cited only for not describing decontamination.

claim: Temperature sampling sets q_l proportional to p_l^(1/τ); τ = 1 is proportional and τ → ∞ uniform; multilingual models used τ from 1.43 to 3.33. UniMax allocates the budget uniformly with a cap of N epochs per language and outperformed temperature sampling across tested scales.
conditions: §3 Eq. 2, Table 1, Algorithm 1, abstract (ICLR 2023). Worked examples in scripts/course/p3_mixtures.py.

claim: Llama 3: final mix about 50% general knowledge, 25% math and reasoning, 17% code, 8% multilingual; annealing on high-quality code and math improved 8B GSM8K/MATH validation by 24.0%/6.4% with negligible gains at 405B; annealing a half-trained 8B over 40B tokens with 30% weight tests data value.

On FLORES-200 devtest (1,012 sentences), token premiums versus English: GPT-2 French 2.0, Chinese 3.15, Hindi 7.41, Khmer 15.18; XLM-R 1.3/0.96/1.25/1.59; Qwen2.5 1.58/1.0/4.42/6.47. GPT-2 gives 1.06 bytes per token on Khmer.
conditions: Measured with Transformers 4.51.3, add_special_tokens=False; scripts/course/p4_tokenization.py with FLORES_DIR set.

claim: Decode(encode(text)) is not the original text for Qwen2.5 on Hindi (NFC normalizer decomposes U+095B) or XLM-R on French (non-breaking spaces) and Khmer (zero-width spaces become spaces); GPT-2 round-trips exactly.
conditions: First 50 FLORES sentences per language; normalizers read from tokenizer.json.

claim: Unigram tokenization prunes a large seed vocabulary by likelihood loss (keeping e.g. top 80% each round and all single characters) and encodes with the Viterbi-best segmentation.

From Llama 3 Table 3, an 8B layer has 41.9M attention and 176.2M SwiGLU parameters (81% MLP); total 8.03B with untied embeddings; KV cache per token in BF16 is 128 KiB with 8 KV heads versus 512 KiB with 32.
conditions: Arithmetic from published configuration; scripts/course/p5_architecture.py.

claim: DeepSeek-V3 has 671B total parameters with 37B activated per token, using 1 shared and 256 routed experts with 8 routed experts per token.
conditions: Abstract; §4.2, p. 22.

claim: A 1,066,112-parameter decoder on Tiny Shakespeare (2,048-token BPE, 600 steps of 2,048 tokens) starts at loss 7.650 (ln V = 7.625) and reaches validation loss 4.13; without warmup 4.44 (ahead until about step 50, then behind); peak lr 3e-2 4.77; 1e-1 5.40; 1e-1 without clipping 5.46 with gradient norms up to 15; resuming at step 300 reproduces the uninterrupted run bit for bit (unrounded per-step losses, final weights, AdamW state); BF16 autocast validation loss equals FP32 to four decimals.
conditions: Executed on Apple M1 CPU with PyTorch 2.6 and Tokenizers 0.21, seed 0; scripts/course/p6_train.py; curves in scripts/course/data/p6_runs.json. Resume test strengthened 2026-11-12: compares unrounded float losses with ==, and final model and optimizer tensors with torch.equal (previously losses rounded to 4 decimals only); rerun on the same CPU.

claim: Chinchilla Approaches 1 and 2 give N_opt ∝ C^0.50 and C^0.49 (Kaplan: 0.73), about 20 tokens per parameter (1B → 20.2B tokens); the published Approach 3 fit implies about 51 tokens per parameter at 1.2e21 FLOPs, which a replication attributes to an unconverged fit and rounding.
conditions: Chinchilla Table 2–3 p. 8, App. D.2 p. 25; Besiroglu et al. abstract; optimum computed in scripts/course/p7_scaling.py.

claim: With large expected inference demand, compute-optimal models are smaller and trained longer than Chinchilla-optimal; quality kept improving up to 10,000 tokens per parameter in the tested runs.
conditions: Abstract only.

claim: Llama 3 fitted N*(C) = A C^α with (α, A) = (0.53, 0.29), predicting 402B on 16.55T tokens at 3.8e25 FLOPs; a two-step forecast from log-likelihood to accuracy slightly underestimated the final ARC Challenge result.
Chinchilla differs from Gopher not only in size and tokens but also in optimizer (AdamW), tokenizer (no NFKC), MassiveText subset mix and FP32 master weights.

Mixed-precision AdamW needs 12 bytes per parameter (BF16 weights and gradients, FP32 moments) or 16 with FP32 master weights; a GPT-style layer at h=4096, a=32, s=4096, b=1 stores about 3.25 GB of activations (2.68 GB attention scores); 70B on 15T tokens on 1,024 H100s at 50% MFU takes about 144 days.
conditions: CS336 lecture 2 figures (989.5 TFLOP/s, 3.35 TB/s); Korthikanti Eq. 1; scripts/course/p8_gpu.py.

claim: With two DDP ranks holding 3 and 1 target tokens, per-rank mean losses give the gradient of the mean of rank means, while dividing summed losses by the all-reduced global count times world size reproduces the single-process token-mean gradient to 3e-8.
conditions: Executed on CPU with gloo, PyTorch 2.6; scripts/course/p9_ddp.py. DDP averages gradients, syncs rank 0 state at construction, 25 MiB default buckets (source read).

claim: ZeroRedundancyOptimizer (ZeRO stage 1) over two gloo ranks holds half of AdamW moments per rank and matches single-process AdamW parameters to 1.2e-6 after 3 steps; checkpointing four blocks reduces bytes saved in forward from 90,112 to 40,960 with identical gradients. FSDP2 fully_shard was not executed (PyTorch 2.6 needs accelerator streams). Communication ratios (DP = stages 1-2 = 2Ψ, stage 3 = 3Ψ) assume ring collectives, 16-bit gradients/weights and one forward-backward per update; with 2 accumulation microbatches the schedule in the post gives 2Ψ, 2Ψ, 3Ψ and 6Ψ. ZeroRedundancyOptimizer itself keeps DDP's full-gradient all-reduce and broadcasts each rank's updated shard.
conditions: Executed on CPU; scripts/course/p10_sharding.py. Stage formulas from ZeRO §5.1–5.3; communication §7.2. ZeRO §7.2.1-7.2.2; the accumulation table is Derived from that schedule. ZeroRedundancyOptimizer collectives read from the PyTorch 2.6 source (_sync_params uses dist.broadcast per rank).

claim: Splitting an MLP first matrix by columns and second by rows across two gloo ranks reproduces the unsplit output to 4e-6 with one all-reduce; splitting the first by rows errs by up to 2.55. Pipeline bubble overhead relative to useful work is (p − 1)/m, (1/v)(p − 1)/m interleaved; the idle share of elapsed time is (p − 1)/(m + p − 1): 3/4 overhead and 3/7 idle for p = m = 4. Tensor-parallel all-reduces occur 4 times per layer per microbatch.
conditions: Executed on CPU; scripts/course/p11_model_parallel.py. Narayanan et al. §2.2–2.3, Takeaway #1 (§3.2). Narayanan et al. define bubble fraction as t_pb/t_id, bubble time over ideal time (§2.2.1, Eq. 1).

claim: DeepSeek-V3 trained with 16-way pipeline, 64-way expert parallelism across 8 nodes and ZeRO-1 data parallelism, without tensor parallelism.

Tiled attention with an online softmax matches ordinary attention to 5e-7; in FlashAttention Fig. 2, GPT-2 medium attention takes 75.2 vs 66.6 GFLOPs but 4.4 vs 40.3 GB HBM traffic and 7.3 vs 41.7 ms on A100.
conditions: Tiling executed on CPU (scripts/course/p12_efficient.py); benchmark quoted from the paper.

claim: With 1,024 values of size about 0.001 and one of 100, FP8 E4M3 with one scale flushes 16% of small values to zero (median relative error 14%); per-128 block scales give 2.1%. DeepSeek-V3 used 1x128 activation tiles and 128x128 weight blocks with relative loss error below 0.25% versus BF16.
conditions: Executed with torch.float8_e4m3fn in PyTorch 2.6; DeepSeek-V3 §3.3, pp. 15–18.

claim: Llama 3 405B ran at 38–43% BF16 MFU on 8K–16K H100s (TP8, CP1 or 16, PP16, DP 8–128, 16M tokens per batch) and had 466 interruptions in 54 days, 419 unexpected, about 78% hardware-related; diurnal 1–2% throughput variation.

Profiling one CPU training step of four nn.TransformerEncoderLayer blocks showed aten::bernoulli_ (default dropout 0.1) at about 30% of self CPU time; disabling dropout cut the profiled step by about a third.
conditions: torch.profiler, PyTorch 2.6, Apple M1; timings vary run to run. scripts/course/p13_at_scale.py.

claim:
The Tülu 3 template renders a user/assistant pair as '<|user|>
What is 2+3?
<|assistant|>
2+3 = 5.<|end_of_text|>'; with assistant-only labels 8 of 25 tokens are trained, including the end-of-text token.
conditions: Executed with Transformers 4.51.3; scripts/course/p14_sft.py.

claim: Tülu 3 SFT ablations (8B): removing WildChat drops AlpacaEval 2 from 12.4 to 7.5; removing safety data drops safety from 93.1 to 74.7; removing math data drops GSM8K from 76.2 to 64.1; seeds vary the average by about 0.1. Averaging the loss per sample under gradient accumulation weighted samples equally; a summed loss fixed it.

With a verifier and independent samples, a prompt survives best-of-K with probability 1-(1-p)^K; with K=16, 1,000 prompts at p=0.5 and 1,000 at p=0.02 yield about 1,000 and 276 kept examples, so hard prompts fall from 50% to 22%.
conditions: Arithmetic and simulation in scripts/course/p15_post_training_data.py; Llama 3 §4.2.2 for rejection sampling with K of 10–30.

claim: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B scored 72.6 on AIME 2024 against 47.0 for Qwen2.5-32B trained with large-scale RL (over 10K steps).
conditions: DeepSeek-R1 arXiv v2, App. F.1, Table 16.

claim: Tülu 3 decontaminates prompts with 8-gram matching: a test item matches if more than 50% of its tokens fall in 8-grams shared with one training example; datasets overlapping more than 2% of an evaluation are removed or filtered; embedding matching was hard to separate from topical similarity.

With reference (0.5, 0.3, 0.2), rewards (0, 1, 2) and beta = 1, the KL-regularized optimum is (0.18, 0.29, 0.53); the DPO gradient on logits for a fresh pair is beta*sigma(-margin)*(e_w - e_l), (0.05, 0, -0.05) at beta = 0.1.
conditions: DPO §4 Eqs. 4–7; checked with autograd in scripts/course/p16_preferences.py.

claim: Tülu 3 found only length-normalized DPO beat its SFT starting point among DPO, SimPO and length-normalized DPO; final 8B beta 5, lr 5e-7. Llama 3 used DPO with lr 1e-5, beta 0.1, masked formatting tokens and an NLL term with coefficient 0.2.
conditions: Tülu 3 §5.4, Tables 18 and 20; Llama 3 §4.1.4.

claim: GRPO normalizes rewards within a group of samples per question, uses no value model and adds KL to the loss; DeepSeekMath used 64 samples, KL 0.04, lr 1e-6 and raised MATH from 46.8% to 51.7%. RL raised Maj@K but not Pass@K. Outcome supervision assigns one advantage per response to all its tokens; equal-reward groups have zero advantage (std-zero convention), leaving only the KL term.

DeepSeek-R1-Zero used rule-based accuracy and format rewards with GRPO, avoided neural reward models for reasoning because of reward hacking, and rose from 15.6% to 77.9% pass@1 on AIME 2024. Tülu 3 RLVR gives reward 10 for verified answers with PPO.

On a four-answer toy, a baseline of 0.2 lowered the variance of a one-sample gradient estimate from 0.102 to 0.057 with the same mean; a group of 8 has mixed rewards with probability 1-p^8-(1-p)^8 (0.34 at p = 0.95).
conditions: Simulation in scripts/course/p17_rl.py.

claim: Tülu 3 persona instruction-following data raised IFEval from 53.6 to 72.8 while IFEval-OOD went from 18.0 to 17.6; length-controlled AlpacaEval raised Spearman correlation with Chatbot Arena from 0.94 to 0.98; optimizing against a proxy reward can lower a gold reward (Gao et al.).
conditions: Tülu 3 Table 32; abstracts of Dubois et al. and Gao et al.

claim: In a simulation where a judge rewards quality + 2 x length and the truth is quality - 0.5 x length^2, best-of-n raises the judge score at every n while true quality peaks at n = 2.
conditions: Illustrative constants; scripts/course/p18_failures.py.

claim: DPO reached about 61% GPT-4 win rate on TL;DR against 57% for PPO; humans preferred DPO samples 58% of the time; on Anthropic HH no public PPO model beat the base model, so best-of-128 stood in for PPO.

With illustrative prices ($3/$15 vs $0.15/$0.60 per million tokens), 1,500 input and 300 output tokens, accuracies 92% vs 85% and $0.50 per error, the larger model costs $49 vs $75 per 1,000 requests; a 95% interval at n = 100 is about ±5 points at 92%.
conditions: Illustrative; scripts/course/p19_choosing.py.

claim: Constrained decoding with a finite-state machine made 1,000 of 1,000 toy generations valid JSON (0 of 1,000 unconstrained); majority voting raises 50% single-sample accuracy to 58% (k=3) and 67% (k=5) when wrong answers are spread over three alternatives. Self-consistency added 17.9 points on GSM8K.
conditions: scripts/course/p20_prompting.py; Wang et al. abstract.

claim: BM25 on a six-passage toy corpus retrieves 2 of 4 gold passages at rank 1 without stemming and 3 with a plural stemmer, failing on a query with no shared words; 8 steps at 95% succeed 66% of the time, 98% with one verified retry per step.
conditions: scripts/course/p21_retrieval.py.

claim: LoRA matched or exceeded full fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B on WikiSQL, MNLI and SAMSum with 4.7M trainable parameters, cut training memory from 1.2 TB to 350 GB, and found rank 1 sufficient for query/value adaptation on those tasks; rank-8 LoRA on Llama 3 8B query and value projections trains 3.4M parameters.
conditions: LoRA Table 4, §4.2, §7.2; parameter count and merging checked in scripts/course/p22_adapt.py.

claim: In standard low-rank settings LoRA substantially underperformed full fine-tuning on programming and mathematics while forgetting less; full fine-tuning learned perturbations of 10-100x higher rank.
conditions: Biderman et al. abstract.

claim: Llama 3 8B in BF16 on an H100 in a bandwidth-only model is bounded at about 209 tokens/s for one sequence (16 GB read per step at 3.35 TB/s); batch 64 at 2,048 tokens of context gives at most about 6,450 tokens/s with a step-time lower bound of 9.9 ms; at most about 60 sequences of 8,192 tokens fit beside BF16 weights; per-channel INT8 scales cut a small channel's error from 74% to 0.8%; speculative decoding yields 3.36 tokens per step at acceptance 0.8 and 4 drafts.
conditions: Bandwidth-only bounds (bytes read at 3.35 TB/s, no compute or overhead): step times are lower bounds and throughputs upper bounds; scripts/course/p23_inference.py; Leviathan et al. Eq. 1.

claim: vLLM (PagedAttention) improved throughput 2-4x at the same latency; GPTQ quantized 175B to 3-4 bits in about four GPU hours with negligible accuracy loss; AWQ protects about 1% salient weights by scaling.
conditions: Abstracts.

claim: Two systems at 85% and 80% on the same 200 items with 20 vs 10 disagreements give a two-sided exact sign-test p = 0.099; the same proportions over 90 disagreements give p = 0.002. LLM judges reach over 80% agreement with humans with position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases.
conditions: scripts/course/p24_evaluating.py; Zheng et al. and Greshake et al. abstracts.

claim: Llama 3 uses a 128K vocabulary (100K tiktoken + 28K non-English) improving English compression from 3.17 to 3.94 characters per token, and GQA with 8 KV heads to reduce KV cache during decoding.

A 224 x 224 image is 196 ViT patches; Mimi in Moshi produces 12.5 frames x 8 codebooks = 100 codec symbols per second, but Moshi's temporal transformer sees 12.5 positions per second, with a depth transformer generating each frame's codebooks; an 8,192-position window is about 82 s only for a hypothetical flattened stream, 655 s in Moshi's layout.
conditions: Mimi and Moshi figures from this site's Moshi review (Moshi §3.3.1, §3.4); scripts/course/p26_modalities.py. The text-to-codec symbol ratio is not used as a compute or KV multiplier.

claim: InstructGPT labelers agreed 72.6% of the time; pairwise agreement is not a ceiling on agreement with individual annotators: two independent annotators each 80% accurate agree 68% of the time while an oracle agrees with each 80%.
conditions: Ouyang et al. §3.4; arithmetic in scripts/course/p16_preferences.py. Replaces a removed claim that label agreement caps model agreement.

claim: At a fixed token budget, a smaller retained corpus means more repeated exposure: 100B tokens over 90B or 30B kept gives about 1.1 or 3.3 passes; FineWeb's filter results hold for its 28B (filters) and 350B (deduplication) token budgets and 1.71B models.
conditions: Arithmetic; FineWeb Sec 3.1. Replaces the removed statement that a strict filter costs nothing in repetition at 100B tokens.

claim: BF16 shares FP32's 8-bit exponent (smallest normal about 1.18e-38), so loss scaling is generally unnecessary, but values below that become subnormal or zero (1e-42 flushes to 0 in PyTorch 2.6 on CPU).
conditions: torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).tiny and a CPU cast, executed 2026-11-12.
